([[Kamloops|Kamloops, British Columbia]]) | college = [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2009–2013) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2013 | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *Consensus first team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013]]) *First team [[Academic All-American]] (2013) *[[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|WCC Player of the Year]] (2013) *First team All-WCC (2013) | stat1label = | stat1value = | stat2label = | stat2value = | stat3label = | stat3value = | letter = | bbr = }} '''Kelly Olynyk''' (born April 19, 1991) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] player at [[Gonzaga University]] and considered a probable first round pick in the [[2013 NBA Draft]]. He moved to Kamloops, B.C. in grade 7.[http://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2013/01/15/kelly_olynyk_emerges_as_star_for_no_8_gonzaga_mens_basketball_team.html Kelly Olynyk emerges as star for No. 8 Gonzaga men’s basketball team] He is currently studying for a [[Master of Business Administration]] at [[Gonzaga University]], having earned a bachelor's degree in [[accounting]] in December 2012, and formerly played basketball for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] before announcing on April 19, his 22nd birthday, that he will skip his senior year and declare for the NBA draft.{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/04/19/gonzagas-kelly-olynyk-declares-for-nba-draft-after-breakout-year/2097545/| title=Gonzaga's Kelly Olynyk declares for NBA draft after breakout year| work=USAToday.com| date=April 19, 2013|accessdate=May 17, 2013}} He also represents the [[Canada national men's basketball team|Canadian national basketball team]]. ==Early life== Olynyk was born into a basketball family. His father Ken was head men's basketball coach at the [[Toronto Varsity Blues|University of Toronto]] from 1989 to 2002 and the Canada junior men's national team from 1983 to 1996, notably cutting future Canadian basketball icon [[Steve Nash]] from the junior national team.{{cite web|url=http://cnnsi.printthis.clickability.com/pt/cpt?expire=&title=IT%27S+A+REALITY+SHOW+THAT%27S+SWEEPING+THE+U.S.%21+PLAYERS+FROM+-+03.18.13+-+SI+Vault&urlID=504680482&action=cpt&partnerID=289881&fb=Y&url=http%3A%2F%2Fsportsillustrated.cnn.com%2Fvault%2Farticle%2Fmagazine%2FMAG1207113%2Findex.htm |title=Canada's Got Talent |first=Kelli |last=Anderson |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |date=March 18, 2013 |accessdate=March 23, 2013}} His mother Arlene was a [[Canadian Interuniversity Sport]] women's basketball referee. From 1995 to 2004, his mother worked for the [[Toronto Raptors]], with one of her jobs being scorekeeper. In 2003,{{cite web|url=http://www.tru.ca/athletics/history/history.html |title=Athletics History |publisher=[[Thompson Rivers University]] |accessdate=March 23, 2013}} Ken became athletic director at [[Thompson Rivers WolfPack|Thompson Rivers University]] in [[Kamloops]], [[British Columbia]], with the rest of the family soon joining him in Kamloops. Unlike many elite Canadian prospects in the early 21st century, he never attended a [[United States|U.S.]] high school or prep school; he instead stayed home at [[South Kamloops Secondary School]], exposing himself to U.S. competition and coaches during summer camps and national team duty. Olynyk developed as a [[point guard]], continuing to play the position even after growing from 6'3" (1.90 m) to 6'10" (2.08 m) in [[Education in Canada#Canada outside Quebec|grade 11]]. ==Gonzaga== He was a 2012–13 first team [[Academic All-America]] selection.{{cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=206473761|title=Olynyk Named To Capital One Academic All-America Team|work=gozags.com|date=February 21, 2013|accessdate=May 17, 2013}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{commonscat}} *[http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=205173776 College bio] {{2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{Canada Squad 2010 FIBA World Championship}} {{Canada Squad FIBA Americas Championship 2011}} {{Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball}} {{Persondata | NAME = Olynyk, Kelly | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = Canadian basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = April 19, 1991 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Olynyk, Kelly}} [[Category:1991 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball people from British Columbia]] [[Category:Basketball people from Ontario]] [[Category:Canadian basketball players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Kamloops]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Toronto]]
